changed: Codex review round 3 on H4, seven findings fixed with regression tests. bash-guard is now parse-or-ask: the deny scan runs on text without quotes and backslashes; shell -c in any option form, eval, source, xargs and -exec ask next to git, a container tool or a variable; variables, substitutions and ANSI-C quoting next to git or docker ask; non-built-in git subcommands (aliases), inline aliases in any case and git pull ask; docker global options ask; docker container <sub> is normalised; every target must be an allowed container; unknown docker subcommands or options ask; compose needs an allowed project. new-task records open, so only close-check closes a task.

rulings.ruling: Any git subcommand outside a built-in list asks, instead of resolving aliases in some git context
rulings.cost_if_wrong: a rarely used built-in that is missing from the list needs one approval

rulings.ruling: docker passes silently only for a table of subcommands and options; everything else asks, including docker run
rulings.cost_if_wrong: ordinary sandbox work outside the table needs approvals until the table grows

rulings.ruling: The H4.R2 ruling that an allowed container named as an option value is an acceptable risk is withdrawn: every target must be allowed and unknown options ask
